title: Fuel Trim Malfunction Bank 1 Advanced
shortDescription: Advanced diagnostic path for long-term fuel trim out of range on Bank 1.
fullDescription:
P0170 sets when the PCM determines fuel trim correction on Bank 1 is outside the normal window at idle, cruise, or load. The advanced path ranks root causes using logged LTFT data across RPM ranges.

The most common causes are vacuum leaks, MAF/MAP errors, and weak fuel delivery. Ignition issues, exhaust leaks, and PCV faults can also contribute.

Root-cause isolation typically starts with a smoke test of the intake and verifying fuel pressure under load.
safetyImpact: Possible hesitation under load; emissions affected.

fixSteps.title: Log fuel trims
fixSteps.instruction: Capture STFT and LTFT at idle and cruise.

fixSteps.title: MAF clean/replace
fixSteps.instruction: Clean with MAF cleaner or replace.

faq.a: It will return — find the cause.

title: Fuel Trim Malfunction Bank 2 Advanced
shortDescription: Advanced diagnostic for fuel trim issue on Bank 2.
fullDescription:
Analogous to P0170 but covers Bank 2. A single-bank fuel trim issue usually points to bank-specific problems: leaking injector, failed O2 sensor, or localized vacuum leak.

Compare bank-to-bank live data to narrow the fault.

title: System Too Lean Bank 2 Advanced
shortDescription: Bank 2 running lean beyond correction limit.
fullDescription:
P0174 advanced path: confirm the lean condition is real by capturing STFT/LTFT totals above 25 percent, then follow the decision tree for unmetered air vs weak fuel delivery.

When only Bank 2 is lean, inspect that side's injectors, intake manifold gaskets, and vacuum hoses.

fixSteps.title: Smoke test Bank 2
fixSteps.instruction: Focus smoke test on that bank.

title: System Too Rich Bank 2 Advanced
fullDescription: P0175 advanced path isolates whether the rich condition is real or sensor-driven. Consider leaking injectors, stuck-open EVAP purge valve, or a failed O2 sensor.

fixSteps.title: Verify via logs
fixSteps.instruction: Log LTFT; confirm negative on Bank 2.

title: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Advanced
fullDescription: P0176 applies to flex fuel vehicles where the ethanol content sensor signals an invalid reading. The advanced path confirms sensor PWM with an oscilloscope.

fixSteps.title: Scope signal
fixSteps.instruction: Capture sensor frequency and pulse width.

title: Fuel Composition Sensor Range/Performance
shortDescription: Fuel composition sensor reading out of range.
fullDescription: P0177 sets when ethanol sensor signal is present but outside believable bounds (e.g., reporting >100 percent ethanol).

title: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Low
fullDescription: P0178 sets when the ethanol sensor input reads below threshold, suggesting short to ground or failed sensor.

title: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit High
fullDescription: P0179 sets when sensor reads above threshold. Typical: open wiring or unplugged sensor.

title: Fuel Tank Temperature Sensor A Circuit Advanced
shortDescription: Fuel tank temp sensor A circuit fault.
fullDescription: P0180 indicates the fuel tank temperature sensor A circuit is reading abnormal. Advanced path verifies sensor resistance versus temperature curve.

title: Fuel Tank Temperature Sensor A Range/Performance
shortDescription: Fuel tank temp sensor range issue.
fullDescription: P0181 sets when reading does not change expectedly with fuel activity or ambient temperature.

title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Advanced
shortDescription: Fuel rail pressure sensor circuit malfunction.
fullDescription:
P0190 sets when the PCM cannot read valid data from the fuel rail pressure sensor. Common on direct injection systems where sensor signal is 0.5-4.5V.

Advanced path confirms reference voltage, ground, and signal on a running engine.

fixSteps.title: Signal check
fixSteps.instruction: Look for proper rail pressure signal.

title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Range/Performance Advanced
shortDescription: Rail pressure signal not tracking commanded.
fullDescription: P0191 sets when the commanded rail pressure and measured rail pressure disagree. Causes include a worn high-pressure pump, failed regulator, or sensor drift.

title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
shortDescription: Fuel rail pressure sensor circuit low voltage.
fullDescription: P0192 sets when sensor output reads below the minimum. Typical cause is a short to ground or sensor failure.

title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit High
shortDescription: Fuel rail pressure sensor reading high.
fullDescription: P0193 sets when sensor voltage exceeds limit, typically open or failed sensor.

title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Intermittent
fullDescription: P0194 sets when sensor signal glitches intermittently. Often caused by loose connector or intermittent wire break.

faq.a: Scope the signal during a drive.

title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Advanced
fullDescription: P0195 sets on an abnormal oil temp reading. Advanced path compares to coolant and intake temps at key-on after soak.

fixSteps.title: Compare to ECT
fixSteps.instruction: Values should be close after soak.

title: Engine Oil Temp Sensor Range/Performance
shortDescription: Oil temp sensor doesn't track expected.
fullDescription: P0196 sets when oil temp reads plausible but does not change as expected with engine operation.

title: Engine Oil Temp Sensor Low Input
shortDescription: Oil temp sensor reads too low.
fullDescription: P0197 sets when oil temp reads low beyond plausibility. Short to ground or open sensor suspected.

title: Engine Oil Temp Sensor High Input
shortDescription: Oil temp sensor reads too high.
fullDescription: P0198 sets with high reading beyond plausibility, typically open circuit.

title: Engine Oil Temp Sensor Intermittent
fullDescription: P0199 sets when oil temp signal glitches. Usually wiring or connector.

title: Injector Circuit/Open Advanced
shortDescription: Advanced diagnostic for injector circuit fault.
fullDescription:
P0200 is set when the PCM detects the injector circuit as a whole is open or has a fault not localized to a specific cylinder. Causes include a broken main injector power wire, blown injector fuse, or PCM driver fault.

Advanced path verifies fuse status, power feed, and then individual injector resistance.

fixSteps.title: Repair
fixSteps.instruction: Address open wire or PCM driver.

title: Glow Plug/Heater Circuit A Advanced
shortDescription: Advanced diagnostic of glow plug circuit A.
fullDescription:
P0380 sets when PCM sees a fault in glow plug control circuit A. On diesel engines this affects cold starting and emissions.

Advanced path measures each glow plug individually with low-amp clamp during pre-heat.
safetyImpact: Hard cold start, high cold emissions.

title: Glow Plug Indicator Circuit Advanced
shortDescription: Glow plug indicator lamp circuit fault.
fullDescription: P0381 sets when the dashboard glow plug indicator lamp control circuit has a fault. Not safety-critical but indicates driver cannot see preheat cycle.
safetyImpact: Cold start may proceed without proper preheat awareness.

fixSteps.title: Bulb/LED check
fixSteps.instruction: Verify indicator operates during bulb check.

title: Glow Plug/Heater Circuit B Advanced
shortDescription: Advanced diagnostic for glow plug circuit B.
fullDescription: P0382 sets for circuit B faults, used on multi-bank diesels with separate glow plug banks.
safetyImpact: Hard cold start on one bank.

title: Glow Plug Relay Control Circuit Advanced
shortDescription: Glow plug relay control circuit malfunction.
fullDescription: P0383 sets when the PCM's glow plug relay control fails to command properly. Common causes are a stuck or failed relay.

title: EGR Flow Malfunction Advanced
shortDescription: Advanced diagnostic for EGR flow issue.
fullDescription:
P0400 sets when EGR flow is insufficient or excessive. Common on diesels and high-mileage gas engines.

Advanced path uses commanded EGR vs delta pressure sensors to isolate carbon buildup vs valve fault.

title: EGR Flow Insufficient Advanced
fullDescription: P0401 advanced path confirms insufficient flow by forcing the EGR valve open with a scan tool while watching intake vacuum or delta pressure.

title: EGR Flow Excessive Advanced
fullDescription: P0402 sets when EGR flow is higher than desired. Causes are a stuck-open valve, debris holding valve off seat, or leaking EGR cooler.
safetyImpact: Rough idle, stalling, high cold emissions.

faq.a: Check for EGR cooler leak on diesels.

title: EGR Control Circuit Advanced
fullDescription: P0403 covers electrical faults in the EGR valve control circuit. Advanced path uses scope to capture control signal.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Fit new valve or repair harness.

title: EGR Position Sensor Range/Performance Advanced
shortDescription: EGR position sensor out of range.
fullDescription: P0404 sets when the EGR position sensor doesn't match commanded position, often due to sensor drift or binding valve.

title: EGR Position Sensor Circuit Low Advanced
fullDescription: P0405 sets with low sensor voltage, typical of short to ground or failed sensor.

title: EGR Position Sensor Circuit High Advanced
fullDescription: P0406 sets when sensor signal is above threshold. Open circuit most common.

title: Catalyst System Efficiency Bank 1 Advanced
fullDescription:
P0420 advanced path confirms true cat degradation versus sensor or upstream root cause. Log upstream and downstream O2 sensor waveforms — the downstream should be relatively flat if the cat is good.

Don't replace the cat until upstream issues (misfires, oil consumption, rich condition) are resolved.

fixSteps.title: Replace cat
fixSteps.instruction: Install new catalytic converter if justified.

title: Malfunction Indicator Lamp Control Circuit Advanced
fullDescription: P0650 sets when the PCM cannot control the MIL properly. Usually an open, short, or failed bulb/driver.

faq.a: Yes — MIL must work for OBD tests.

title: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit Advanced
fullDescription: P0651 sets when the 5V reference circuit B is abnormal. Multiple sensors will be affected. Usually a shorted sensor pulling the reference down.
safetyImpact: Multiple sensor faults; limp mode likely.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect sensors
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect one at a time to find short.

title: Sensor Reference Voltage B Low
fullDescription: P0652 sets when the B reference is pulled below spec. Look for shorted sensor or shorted wiring.

title: Sensor Reference Voltage B High
fullDescription: P0653 sets when reference B voltage is above spec, implying open or short to power.

title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Bank 1 Advanced
fullDescription: P0660 sets when the intake manifold runner/tuning valve control on Bank 1 does not match commanded state. Common on V engines with variable intake geometry.

faq.a: Power may suffer but safe to drive.

title: Glow Plug Control Module Control Circuit Advanced
shortDescription: Glow plug control module circuit fault.
fullDescription: P0670 sets when the PCM cannot communicate with or control the glow plug control module. Common on modern diesels with dedicated GPCM.

title: Glow Plug Cylinder 1 Circuit Advanced
fullDescription: P0671 isolates a fault to the cylinder 1 glow plug. Usually the plug itself is open, or the feed wire has broken.

title: Glow Plug Cylinder 2 Circuit Advanced
fullDescription: Same as P0671 but for cylinder 2.

title: Glow Plug Cylinder 3 Circuit Advanced
fullDescription: Same as P0671 but for cylinder 3.

title: Glow Plug Cylinder 4 Circuit Advanced
fullDescription: Same as P0671 but for cylinder 4.

title: Glow Plug Cylinder 5 Circuit Advanced
fullDescription: P0675 isolates to cyl 5, common on inline-5 and V10 diesels.

title: Glow Plug Cylinder 6 Circuit Advanced
fullDescription: Same as P0675 for cylinder 6.

title: Glow Plug Cylinder 7 Circuit Advanced
fullDescription: Same as P0675 for cylinder 7. V8 diesels.

faq.a: Risk on stuck plugs; use penetrating oil.

title: Glow Plug Cylinder 8 Circuit Advanced
fullDescription: Same as P0675 for cylinder 8.

title: PCM Power Relay Control Circuit Open
shortDescription: PCM power relay control circuit open.
fullDescription: P0685 sets when the PCM's main relay control line shows open circuit. Often caused by relay failure or harness break.

fixSteps.title: Relay test
fixSteps.instruction: Bench test or swap with identical relay.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Fit new relay or repair wire.

title: PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Advanced
shortDescription: PCM power relay sense circuit abnormal.
fullDescription: P0688 sets when the PCM sense line does not match the commanded relay state. Diagnosing typically requires scoping both control and sense lines.

fixSteps.title: Repair
fixSteps.instruction: Replace relay or repair sense wire.

title: PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit High
fullDescription: P0690 sets with high voltage on the sense line when it should be low. Typical open or stuck-on relay.

faq.a: Yes if stuck on — address promptly.

title: Fan 1 Control Circuit Low Advanced
fullDescription: P0691 sets when fan 1 control pulls low unexpectedly or is shorted to ground. Fan may run constantly.
safetyImpact: Battery drain; possible overheating if fan stuck off.
symptoms: Fan runs constantly or not at all

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Fit new fan assembly or relay.

faq.a: Yes if fan doesn't run in traffic.

title: Fan 1 Control Circuit High Advanced
fullDescription: P0692 sets when fan 1 control reads high when it should be low, typical of an open circuit.

faq.a: Only short distance; risk of overheat.

title: Fan 2 Control Circuit Low Advanced
fullDescription: P0693 sets on the secondary cooling fan circuit low. Many vehicles use dual-speed or dual-fan setups.

fixSteps.title: Repair
fixSteps.instruction: Fix short or replace fan module.

title: Fan 2 Control Circuit High Advanced
fullDescription: P0694 sets on an open fan 2 circuit.

faq.a: Possibly — overheating if main fan also struggles.

title: Clutch Actuator Circuit/Open Advanced
fullDescription: P0900 sets when the clutch actuator (DCT/AMT) circuit reads open. Without command, the clutch cannot engage/disengage under PCM control.

title: Clutch Actuator Circuit Range/Performance Advanced
shortDescription: Clutch actuator response out of range.
fullDescription: P0901 sets when actuator performance lags the command. Common with clutch wear or hydraulic contamination.

title: Clutch Actuator Circuit Low
fullDescription: P0902 sets with low voltage on actuator control, suggesting short to ground.

title: Clutch Actuator Circuit High
fullDescription: P0903 sets with high voltage on the actuator circuit, suggesting open control or disconnected plug.

title: Gate Select Position Circuit
fullDescription: P0905 sets on AMT units when the gate select actuator position sensor fails. Without it, transmission cannot select gate before engaging gear.

title: Gate Select Control Circuit
fullDescription: P0910 sets when the control for the gate select actuator has electrical issues.

title: Gear Shift Position Circuit
fullDescription: P0915 sets when gear shift position sensor readings are abnormal. Affects AMT, DCT, and some shift-by-wire systems.

title: Gear Shift Forward Actuator Circuit
fullDescription: P0920 sets when the forward shift actuator circuit has issues. Prevents normal forward gear engagement in AMT/DCT.

title: Gear Shift Reverse Actuator Circuit
fullDescription: P0925 sets when the reverse shift actuator circuit is faulty. Reverse engagement may not occur.
